Choose the SDK when you own the host

orca-harness-sdk is the high-level Rust facade for embedding Orca Harness in your own process. It composes models, workspace tools, sessions, memory, skills, MCP, subagents, workflows, events, retries, truncation, and cancellation without importing the orcacode terminal UI or its configuration layer.

HOST RESPONSIBILITY

The SDK executes with the permissions of your process. Your application owns credential loading, approvals, configuration, process isolation, shutdown, and the set of exposed tools. A ToolPolicy authorizes registered calls; it is not an operating-system sandbox.

ChooseWhen
orca-harness-sdkYou want a batteries-included Rust composition API with sessions and common extensions.
orca-harness-coreYou need direct control over the minimal model → tool loop and will assemble every lifecycle component yourself.
orcacodeYou want the ready-made interactive or headless terminal host rather than an embedded library.

Follow a focused guide

The SDK documentation is split by the host behavior you are building. Start with the first-agent guide, then add only the lifecycle components your application needs.

GuideWhat it covers
First agent →Install the crate, configure a provider, add tools and policy, observe events, and choose ephemeral, persistent, or imported session context.
Host assembly →Compose memory, skills, MCP, processes, subagents, workflows, retries, truncation, and evidence-based verification.
Background lifecycle →Drain run events, distinguish detached work, process completions, continue a conversation, cancel safely, and shut down.

Supported model adapters

Harness::agent accepts any implementation of the re-exported Model trait. Credentials are host inputs: the SDK does not read Orcacode’s saved configuration or launch an interactive login flow.

AdapterConstruction
AnthropicAnthropicModel::new("model").api_key(key)
OpenAI or compatibleOpenAiModel::new("model").api_key(key); add .base_url(url) for a compatible endpoint.
OpenRouterOpenRouterModel::new("provider/model").api_key(key)
ChatGPT/CodexOpenAiCodexModel::new("model", credential_source); the host owns acquisition, persistence, and refresh.
Custom or test modelImplement Model. Repository examples use scripted models for deterministic offline tests.

Run the checked-in examples

The repository examples are executable documentation. Most use scripted models and temporary workspaces; live_host_assembly intentionally makes real provider calls.

$ cargo run -p orca-harness-sdk --example custom_tool_events
$ cargo run -p orca-harness-sdk --example session_lifecycle
$ cargo run -p orca-harness-sdk --example host_assembly
$ cargo run -p orca-harness-sdk --example background_cancellation
$ cargo run -p orca-harness-sdk --example recovery_compaction_retry

See crates/sdk/examples/agent_tour.rs for a broad single-file tour and crates/sdk/examples/live_host_assembly.rs for a fully composed live host. Validate SDK targets with cargo test -p orca-harness-sdk and cargo clippy -p orca-harness-sdk --all-targets -- -D warnings.
